newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Dutch PM urges common sense in Albania crisis.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PM urges common sense in Albania crisis.

text.p: Dutch premier Wim Kok, whose country holds the EU presidency, urged Albanian leaders on Thursday to show common sense and said there was no alternative to a political solution to the Balkan state's crisis.

"I hope that common sense will be used by the Albanian leadership in order to contribute to political solutions -- there is no acceptable alternative for that," he told a news conference during an official visit to the Czech Republic.
Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo is due to fly to the Albanian capital Tirana on Friday, after earlier visiting Italy and Greece.

"The EU has to be active now in getting a sufficient amount of information and to see how we can contribute to a political solution, because the use of violence and use of arms is always a very bad way to solve a problem," Kok said after talks with Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.
He said he was concerned that part of Albania was split between areas under the control of President Sali Berisha and parts under the control of other forces.
"That can easily lead to an escalation of the use of power and the use of violence. Our first priority is to contribute to a political solution," he added.
Anger over the failure of pyramid investment schemes has spread across the country and armed insurgents hold some towns in the south.
Western states have mounted a campaign to end the violence which has killed at least 20 people.
Klaus said Albania had previously appeared to be coping well with the transformation from its former isolation.
"I am very sad that the situation has changed and I am hoping it will be solved quickly," he said.

A delegation from the Council of Europe, a pan-European organisation which promotes democracy and human rights, was due to hold talks in Albania and the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said on Tuesday that former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky would travel to the country to assess the situation.
